hint: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them.
hint: You can do so by running one of the following commands sometime before
hint: your next pull:
hint:
hint:   git config pull.rebase false  # merge
hint:   git config pull.rebase true   # rebase
hint:   git config pull.ff only       # fast-forward only
hint:
hint: You can replace "git config" with "git config --global" to set a default
hint: preference for all repositories. You can also pass --rebase, --no-rebase,
hint: or --ff-only on the command line to override the configured default per
hint: invocation.
User just pasted git hint. Likely wants explanation. Provide guidance.

It looks like you ran `git pull` in a repository that has diverging commits on the remote and local branches. Git is telling you that it doesn’t know how you’d like to reconcile those differences, and it’s giving you three common strategies:

| Strategy | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| **Merge** (`git config pull.rebase false`) | Creates a new *merge commit* that combines the two histories. Your local branch stays on its own line, and a new commit records the merge point. |
| **Rebase** (`git config pull.rebase true`) | Re‑writes your local commits on top of the updated remote branch, giving you a linear history. No merge commit is created. |
| **Fast‑forward only** (`git config pull.ff only`) | Only updates your branch if the remote can be fast‑forwarded. If there’s any divergence, `git pull` will refuse to merge or rebase and you’ll have to resolve it manually. |

### How to choose

| Scenario | Recommended strategy |
|----------|----------------------|
| You want a clean, linear history (e.g., for feature branches that will be squashed later) | `rebase` |
| You’re fine with merge commits and want to preserve the exact branching structure | `merge` |
| Your workflow requires that pulls never create merge commits and you want to be alerted if a fast‑forward isn’t possible | `ff only` |

### Setting the default

You can set this preference globally or per‑repo:

```bash
# Per‑repository (only affects the current repo)
git config pull.rebase true          # or false / ff only

# Globally (affects all repos you work with)
git config --global pull.rebase true
```

If you ever want to override the default for a single pull, just add an option:

```bash
git pull --rebase          # temporary rebase
git pull --no-rebase       # temporary merge
git pull --ff-only         # temporary fast‑forward only
```

### Quick fix for the current situation

If you just want to pull right now and don’t care about the strategy, you can run:

```bash
git pull --rebase   # or --no-rebase / --ff-only as needed
```

Once you’ve pulled, it’s a good idea to decide on the strategy that fits your workflow and set it so you won’t see the warning again. Happy coding!
